events.subject_response: Vecchio did not respond to WTTW News's request for comment about the termination recommendation. His defense attorney, Thomas Mahoney, declined comment to WTTW News; the Chicago Sun-Times reported Mahoney said Vecchio had a young child he supported financially when opposing continued detention. No denial of the alleged conduct was reported.
events.summary: WTTW News reported that Vecchio was arrested and charged with felony aggravated domestic battery after prosecutors accused him of punching, kneeing, choking, and preventing a woman described as his girlfriend from leaving. Cook County Circuit Judge Kimberly Przekota ordered him held pending trial. The report also documented Chicago Police Board and COPA findings/recommendations that he be fired for false statements and improper traffic-stop searches; the disciplinary outcome is not final.
